_help: Student journeys for journeys.html: anonymous stories of how a kid at Maho has grown, told by their volunteer teacher. Edit on GitHub (pencil icon), then commit: the site republishes itself. One journey = one { } block, separated by commas. NEVER a child's name or nickname, age, class or grade, photo, or anything else that could identify them (Juvenile Justice Act, Section 74): write 'a student', 'he' or 'she'. Every real journey needs the shelter's written OK for that story: put the month you got it in "shelterConsent" (like "2026-11"). "teacher" is optional: the volunteer who tells the story, only if they agree to be named. There are no photos on this page, on purpose. While any journey has "placeholder": true, the page stays out of search results: replace the placeholder blocks as real journeys come in.

journeys.title: Finding his focus
journeys.before: After my first class with him, I thought it would take a long time to get him to sit through an entire class as he was full of energy and loved moving around and playing with others.
journeys.after: However, as the classes progressed, I noticed a significant change in him. We established a set of classroom rules, which he genuinely respected and followed. There were a few instances when he doubted his ability to speak English but I guess a few words of encouragement from me and others at the NGO made a difference. He has made some really good progress and I am sure he will do wonders in whatever he decides to pursue!

journeys.title: From quiet to confident
journeys.before: When I first met him, he was a very quiet kid who wasn't really interested in learning or interacting, and I used to be the only one talking, which made it quite difficult to teach him.
journeys.after: But eventually, I started learning about his interests and using them to teach, which helped him enjoy the subject and open up to me even more. Since then he has started coming up to me on his own to talk and even volunteering to answer in class. His journey from coming out of his shell to becoming a confident child is truly inspiring and has made him a much better learner.
